newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm as Fed stands pat on rates.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm as Fed stands pat on rates.

text.p: Chilean shares closed higher on Tuesday after news the Federal Reserve had decided to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged at its policy meeting in Washington, traders said.

The bolsa is closed Wednesday for a public holiday and will reopen at 0930 local time on Thursday. Stocks are seen extending their advance at the opening, with the market expected to reflect any further gains on Wall Street on Wednesday, they said.
The 40-share .IPSA index closed up 0.67 percent at 121.92 points.
The general .IGPA index gained 0.33 percent to 5,401.27 points in turnover of 15.2 billion pesos worth of shares.
"Orders increased noticeably as soon as news of the Fed's decision was out," one dealer said.

The bolsa also benefited from a rally in the electricity sector, which rose for a second day amid expectations that weekend rains spelled the end of a drought that has depleted the reservoirs of hydroelectric generators, traders said.
Government figures show the rainfall brought water levels at the Colbun and Rapel dams, owned by Endesa SA, back to normal.
But Endesa's Laja reservoir -- the largest in central Chile-- is still operating at four percent of capacity.
Endesa climbed 0.57 percent to 264-1/2 pesos, while its parent company Enersis rose 1.9 percent at 268-1/2 pesos.

Declining issues included supermarket group Unimarc, down 1.31 percent at 151 pesos, copper products maker Madeco, down 0.91 percent at 1,085 pesos, and telecommunications company CTC, which shed 0.61 percent to 3,270 pesos.
